title: Throughput commitment metric proposal & autoscale failsafe ladder
creator: Riley Chen
description: Draft an operational and contractual definition for Dedicated throughput commitments that: (1) specifies a measurable throughput metric for contracts, (2) maps error budget consumption to graduated remediation and crediting, and (3) defines an autoscale/priority failsafe ladder for fleet controls during constrained capacity. This ticket will produce a single source-of-truth doc for legal + sales and a companion technical spec for engineering to instrument measurement and enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: A clear, testable throughput metric (primary + fallbacks) suitable for inclusion in an SOW and enforcement code
An error-budget model that ties measured shortfalls to proportional credits, with worked examples for common failure modes
A deterministic autoscale failsafe ladder describing routing/priority changes and customer notification windows
Legal review sign-off on contract language snippets and notice windows
Engineering checklist for telemetry, alerts, and automated credit computation PRs linked
decision_log: 2026-03-06: Chose tokens/sec-per-tenant (quantile-adjusted) as the primary metric after weighing tokens/min and RPS. Rationale: tokens align to billing units and captures model size variance.
2026-03-08: Agreed to include a 1-hour burst allowance (burst window) that does not count toward sustained throughput guarantees but consumes a separate burst bucket.

2026-03-10: Decided on a three-tier remediation ladder: (1) automated autoscale + cost-burst, (2) temporary prioritized routing + regional failover, (3) credits and contract remediation. Legal prefers explicit notice windows for tiers 2 and 3.
comments: 2026-03-06 Riley Chen: Initial draft posted. Incl. metric proposals, burst-window sketch, and sample credit formula. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/throughput-proposal-867530

2026-03-07 Marco Alvarez (ENG): Engineering feedback: need to instrument per-tenant 95th tokens/sec quantile and a separate burst-bucket counter. Also flagged KV-cache warmup as source of transient degradation for first 30 minutes after deployment.
